- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast modestly to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is erratic, apply smoothing: average last 3–5 forecast values before final output.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward.  
- If sentiment is neutral or weak (0.2–0.6) and forecast is drifting, align with recent 18-day moving average.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of 30-day low if sentiment is positive — may indicate market overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is rising and forecast is falling, reverse direction slightly — sentiment may be driving a rebound.
